description: Ribollita is a hearty Tuscan bread and vegetable soup, truly a classic of Italian cucina povera. Its name, meaning 'reboiled', refers to the traditional method of reheating the soup the day after it is made, allowing the flavors to deepen beautifully. This rustic dish is perfect for a comforting meal, especially during colder months.

instructions.title: Prepare the Soffritto
instructions.text: Heat the olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the chopped onion, carrots, and celery. Cook gently for about 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are softened and translucent. Do not let them brown.

instructions.title: Add Garlic and Tomatoes
instructions.text: Stir in the minced garlic and cook for another 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Be careful not to burn the garlic. Pour in the crushed tomatoes and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 5 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.

instructions.title: Simmer with Broth and Beans
instructions.text: Add the vegetable broth and the drained cannellini beans to the pot. Bring the soup to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and let it simmer for 15 minutes to allow the flavors to develop.

instructions.title: Incorporate Greens
instructions.text: Add the chopped cavolo nero (Tuscan kale) and shredded green cabbage to the simmering soup. Stir well, ensuring the greens are submerged. Continue to simmer for another 10-15 minutes, or until the kale and cabbage are tender.

instructions.title: Build the Soup Layers
instructions.text: Remove the soup from the heat. In an oven-safe casserole dish, alternate layers of the vegetable soup with slices of stale Tuscan bread. Start with a layer of soup, then a layer of bread, and repeat, ending with a layer of soup on top. Gently press down.

instructions.title: The 'Twice Boiled' Stage
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 180 degrees Celsius (350 degrees Fahrenheit). Place the casserole dish in the oven and bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the top is slightly crusty and golden and the bread has absorbed much of the liquid. Alternatively, for a more traditional 'reboiled' method, let the soup cool completely and refrigerate overnight. Reheat gently on the stovetop the next day, stirring occasionally.

instructions.title: Serve and Garnish
instructions.text: Let the Ribollita rest for a few minutes before serving. Ladle generous portions into bowls. Drizzle with a good quality extra virgin olive oil and season with freshly ground black pepper. Optionally, sprinkle with grated Parmigiano Reggiano cheese.

tips: For the best Ribollita, use genuinely stale Tuscan bread. If fresh bread is all you have, toast it lightly in the oven to dry it out before layering.
The 'twice boiled' aspect is key. While you can eat it fresh, allowing the soup to cool and reheating it the next day significantly deepens and melds the flavors.
Do not overcook the vegetables in the initial soffritto; they should be soft but not browned. This ensures a clean, sweet base for the soup.
